questions.question: What marks the end of an episode as an "abandonment"?
options: The model producing a final answer
A guardrail tripping or the model explicitly saying it cannot complete the task
The context window filling to its limit
questions.explanation: See the "From a single call to a full task: what an episode is" section: delivery ends when the final answer is emitted; abandonment ends when a guardrail trips or the model says it cannot complete the task — both end the episode, but the engineering follow-up is very different.

questions.question: The model only has the right to request an action. Who owns whether the parameters are legal, whether to execute, and what happens on failure?
options: The model, inside the same tool_use generation
The client — which runs the code, validates, and handles failures
The user, who signs off every step
questions.explanation: See the "The loop's three beats: thought, action, observation" section: the model only emits the tool_use block; the code is yours to run. Whether the parameters are legal, whether to execute, and how to handle failures are all the client's concern.

questions.question: Because every extra turn resends all prior context, what happens as the context thickens?
options: The model automatically compresses its history
Input cost grows roughly quadratically with turn count, and the model's grip on early content degrades
The output token count doubles every turn
The context window limit automatically expands
questions.explanation: See the "How context grows inside the loop" section: cumulative input tokens grow roughly quadratically, so cost and latency climb with it; as context thickens the model's grip on early content weakens — showing up as repeated actions and forgotten data.
